prompt.context: Our firm has just wrapped up a project with The Stance School, which offers K-12 education in Philadelphia, to help them with developing two major strategic initiatives. The first initiative, which is the priority, is an e-learning platform for their students to facilitate remote learning, in response to a global pandemic that resulted in students having to take classes from home for the last few months of the school year. The other initiative is a professional development tool to help the teachers with developing and effectively providing a remote curriculum to the students. The team that worked on the strategic planning determined that the cost would be $1M.
prompt.question: You are now tasked with determining how these initiatives will be funded within the next year and whether or not the school should move forward with this project.

clarifying_info.a: Currently it is 2020 H1. The initiatives will be launched at the start of the 2020-2021 school year. The last income statement we have is from FY 2018.

clarifying_info.q: Is this a public or private school?
clarifying_info.a: The school is a private school in a major metropolitan city in the US.
The school consists of a lower and upper school, educating levels K-12.
There are 1,000 students in the school. Students are primarily middle-upper middle class.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of students are on scholarship?
clarifying_info.a: Approximately 10% of the students are on scholarship.

clarifying_info.q: Do we need to consider ongoing costs for the program?
clarifying_info.a: No need to consider ongoing costs. With the $1M in savings per year, that should also cover the ongoing run-rate of the initiatives.

clarifying_info.q: Can the school use its endowment to fund this?
clarifying_info.a: The endowment is allocated for specific purposes and to ensure the school is funded long-term. The endowment would not be an option for funding the initiatives.

exhibits.title: Income Statement Line Items (FY 2018)
exhibits.shows: A comparative income statement for The Stance School and two competitor schools (Rittenhouse Prep and Chestnut Hill Day School), with a footnote that grants are not allocated to school expenses and that The Stance School is currently receiving 100% of eligible grants.

exhibits.title: Stance Tuition and Enrollment Information, with Benchmarks to Competitor Schools
exhibits.shows: Two line charts covering 2015-2019. The left chart shows annual tuition trends for Stance, Rittenhouse Prep, and Chestnut Hill Day School. The right chart shows annual enrollment trends for the same three schools.

exhibits.title: Positions, Salaries, Headcount, with Benchmarks to Competitor Schools
exhibits.shows: A table listing all staff positions at The Stance School with annual salary, current headcount, and average headcount at competitor schools.

exhibits.title: Benchmark Ratio of Students to Headcount (5 Selected Positions)
exhibits.shows: A table for 5 specific positions showing salary, current headcount, and a benchmark ratio of students to headcount that the school is targeting.

framework: Internal Opportunities — Raise Cash: increase tuition; grow alumni giving
Internal Opportunities — Cut Costs: reduce CAPEX (capital expenditures); reduce OPEX (operating expenditures including salaries)
External Opportunities — Public Sector: lobby to raise federal/state appropriations; apply for additional grants
External Opportunities — Private Sector: solicit donations; raise endowment contributions; pursue loans
Note: a profit tree (revenue vs. cost) is equally appropriate as an alternative framework

questions.prompt: What conclusions or insights can be drawn from examining The Stance School and its competitors' line items? (Exhibits 1 & 2)
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare Stance's expenses as a proportion of Tuition & Fees to competitors, not in absolute terms. Key insights: (1) Stance cannot raise tuition further — it already has the highest tuition and enrollment has been declining as tuition rose, suggesting price-sensitive families have left for competitors. (2) Stance is already receiving 100% of eligible grants (Footnote on Exhibit 1), so grant revenue cannot increase. (3) On a proportional basis, Salaries/Wages/Benefits are the largest expense and appear out of line with competitor ratios. Scholarships are the second-largest expense, but reducing them would cost the school grant funding. Conclusion: the fastest path to $1M is cost-cutting, specifically staffing, rather than revenue growth.

math.setup: Express each Stance expense as % of Stance Tuition & Fees ($35M), then compare to same ratio for competitors. E.g., Salaries: Stance = 12,250/35,000 = 35%; Rittenhouse = 3,625/14,500 = 25%; Chestnut Hill = 6,670/29,000 = 23%.
steps: Stance Student Services: 5,250/35,000 = 15%; Rittenhouse: 2,175/14,500 = 15%; Chestnut Hill: 3,480/29,000 = 12%
Stance Salaries: 12,250/35,000 = 35%; Rittenhouse: 3,625/14,500 = 25%; Chestnut Hill: 6,670/29,000 = 23% → Stance is significantly over-indexed
Stance Scholarships: 10,500/35,000 = 30%; Rittenhouse: 5,800/14,500 = 40%; Chestnut Hill: 11,600/29,000 = 40% → Stance is under-indexed here
Stance Maintenance: 7,000/35,000 = 20%; Rittenhouse: 2,900/14,500 = 20%; Chestnut Hill: 7,250/29,000 = 25% → roughly in line
math.answer: Salaries are the primary expense out of line with competitors (~35% of tuition vs. ~24% at peers). Tuition cannot be raised (highest in market, enrollment declining). Grants are maxed out. Cost-cutting in staffing is the logical focus.

questions.prompt: The school has determined these are the 5 positions to reduce. Calculate the annual cost savings if the school matches the benchmark ratio of students to position for each of the 5 positions. (Exhibit 4; 1,000 students total)
questions.guidance: Candidate divides 1,000 students by each benchmark ratio to find the target headcount, subtracts from current headcount to find reductions, then multiplies by salary. Strong candidates note the total falls $90K short of the $1M goal and pivot to asking how to close the gap.

math.setup: Target headcount = 1,000 ÷ benchmark ratio. Reduction = current headcount − target headcount. Savings = reduction × salary.
steps: Admin Assistant: target = 1,000/500 = 2; reduce by 1; savings = 1 × $45,000 = $45,000
Guidance Counselor: target = 1,000/100 = 10; reduce by 5; savings = 5 × $65,000 = $325,000
IT Technician: target = 1,000/200 = 5; reduce by 1; savings = 1 × $60,000 = $60,000
math.answer: $910,000 in annual savings — $90,000 short of the $1M goal.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the potential risks and associated costs you anticipate when eliminating these roles?

categories.name: Financial Costs
ideas: Pension obligations or early exit costs
Union negotiation costs and potential delays
Legal fees related to employment terminations

categories.name: Non-Financial / Operational Costs
ideas: Time required to eliminate roles may delay savings realization within the budget year
Negative PR associated with publicizing layoffs at a school
Potential decline in enrollment if student-to-staff ratios visibly worsen
Negative outcomes for student mental health if counselor or support staff ratios drop
Remaining staff morale and potential turnover among retained employees
Risk of work being redistributed onto teachers, degrading instructional quality

brainstorming.prompt: What are some ways that The Stance School could close the remaining $90,000 funding gap to reach the $1M goal?

categories.name: Public/Government Sources
ideas: Lobby for additional state or federal appropriations tied to pandemic relief or digital learning
Apply for COVID-related education grants from federal programs (e.g., ESSER funds)

categories.name: Revenue from New Platforms
ideas: License the e-learning platform or teacher professional development tool to other schools for a fee
Offer remote tutoring or supplemental courses on the platform to external students for a fee

categories.name: Private Fundraising
ideas: Solicit donations from current parents and alumni via a targeted campaign
Identify high-net-worth alumni and offer naming rights (rooms, awards, scholarships) in exchange for major gifts
Corporate sponsorships or partnerships tied to the e-learning initiative

categories.name: Internal Adjustments
ideas: Identify smaller non-salary cost reductions (supplies, contracts, discretionary spend)
Defer lower-priority CAPEX to redirect funds toward the initiative

recommendation: Move forward with the project: eliminate the 5 targeted roles to generate $910K in annual savings, and close the remaining $90K gap through alternative funding sources (donations, licensing revenue, government appropriations, or minor additional cost cuts).
Alternative: do not move forward until the school achieves full cost alignment with benchmarks, recognizing that proceeding with a funding gap carries execution risk.
risks: Negative PR from layoffs could harm the school's reputation and community trust
Decline in enrollment if reduced student-staff ratios are perceived negatively, which would reduce tuition revenue and compound the problem
Negative performance implications for students if support services are stretched (less likely for non-teaching roles)
Missing out on critical technology modernization if the project is delayed — teachers and students remain disadvantaged in a remote learning environment
Morale and retention risk among remaining staff
next_steps: Ensure no negative impact to enrollments before and after role eliminations, as tuition is the primary revenue driver
Begin contract reviews and formal process of eliminating the 5 roles to finalize budget and savings reallocation for the next school year
Conduct an in-depth analysis on the pros and cons of each specific role elimination, including legal and HR sequencing
Identify and pursue additional revenue opportunities (licensing, donations, grants) to close the $90K gap
